thread:
marie: Heads-up: Sales flagged a customer pushing to convert to a smaller tier mid-year and asks for credits vs penalties. Need alignment on whether we offer a "soft floor" (rollover credits) or a "hard cap" (ETF) approach.
devon: Operationally hard caps are easier to enforce. Soft floors mean we have to track rollover buckets and reconcile usage which complicates billing and forecasting.
anya: UX tradeoff: soft floor is friendlier and reduces churn but adds perceived product complexity. Could we offer soft floor only for 1st-year pilots?
samir: Billing thoughts: two models: (A) Rollover credits: unused committed capacity converts to credits at end of billing period and applied to next period; (B) Shortfall ETF: compute shortfall over 30d and charge `shortfall_units * unit_price * haircut`.
liz: Legal prefers deterministic math. Rollover rules require precise expiry windows and dispute resolution. If we do credits, cap expiry to 90 days and show ledger entries.
finance-bot: Simulation: customer profile A (25k tokens/day commit) shows churn reduction ~12% with rollover but ARR hit vs baseline ~-6% unless we reduce credits value (e.g., convert at 80% of unit price).
clara: Customer success: clients love rollover in demos. But sales warns of abuse if credits are tradable between orgs. We must restrict credits to the original subscription.
marie: Proposed hybrid: offer a single 30d rollover for pilots with credits valued at 80% of list (to protect ARR). For enterprise annuals, allow quarterly shrink up to 25% w/o fee; beyond that ETF applies.
devon: Implementation note: need `rollover_credits_balance`, `rollover_expiry_ts`, and non-transferable flag in the ledger. API to return `estimated_fee` on downsize request.
anya: UI: add a new tile on Billing page that shows `Rollover credits: 120,000 tokens (expires in 21d)` and an explainer tooltip. On downgrade modal show projected credits used and remaining shortfall.
samir: Example ETF calc (put in T&C):
```
shortfall_units = max(0, committed_units - actual_units_last_30d)
shortfall_fee = shortfall_units * unit_price * haircut_percentage
example: committed=750k tokens, actual=500k tokens -> shortfall=250k; fee = 250k * $0.0002 * 0.25 = $12.5
```
liz: We'll draft two clause variants: one for pilot-friendly rollover (explicit expiry + 80% valuation + no transfer) and one for enterprise shrink (quarterly cap + ETF formula). I'll also add sample tables.
finance-bot: Action: I'll produce a 3-scenario P&L (rollover @80%, rollover @100%, ETF @25%) by EOD.
marie: Launch gating: legal clause, finance P&L, ledger schema, UI mock, and migration plan for current pilot customers.
clara: Migration: propose auto-convert existing pilot unused credits to `rollover_credits` with 90d expiry and notify customers.
devon: Tech debt: add tests for ledger idempotency and admin ability to revoke credits in breach cases.
anya: UX owner will deliver mocks by Thu; Samir please include the T&C examples inline so we can validate copy.
samir: Will draft both clause variants and examples today.
marie: OK, we'll record this under Roadmap > Pricing Controls > "Shrink & Rollover" and pause tier cut until legal + finance signoff. Ping me if you need edge-case scenarios. :white_check_mark:
